title: The confident method
context: A developer asked an AI assistant to deep-clone a settings object before mutating it inside a reducer. The suggested code runs the import fine but throws the moment the function is actually called.
question: What happens when updateSettings runs?
options: TypeError: _.deepClone is not a function — Lodash's deep-clone method is named cloneDeep, not deepClone.
The settings object clones correctly but the patch is applied in the wrong order.
Object.assign throws because draft is undefined at that point.
The function works correctly; there is no bug here.

explanation.theBug: Lodash does not export a deepClone function. Its actual deep-clone method is named cloneDeep. Calling _.deepClone(...) throws TypeError: _.deepClone is not a function the moment this code path runs, because _.deepClone is undefined on the Lodash object.
explanation.whyAIGeneratesThis: LLMs learn API names statistically from a mix of libraries and blog posts, some of which really do define hand-rolled utilities called deepClone. The model blends the common English phrase 'deep clone' with Lodash's general naming style and produces a plausible-sounding method name that Lodash simply never shipped.

theFix.commentary: Lodash's real deep-clone export is cloneDeep — check the docs or type definitions before trusting an AI-suggested method name.

explanation.reviewHeuristic: When AI code calls a library method you don't recognize, look it up before merging — a plausible name is not the same as a real export.
